articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of cosmic hydrogen clustering, revolutionizing how astronomers map the large-scale structure of the universe.

articles.title: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
articles.description: The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image was the work of hundreds of scientists and captured the first direct view of a black hole's shadow—becoming one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. A team of four from CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, has developed a powerful new imaging technique that validated the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Independent analysis confirms the landmark 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of M87*, the first direct photograph of a black hole. This validation strengthens our understanding of these cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Earliest known compact quasar pair poses a black hole growth puzzle
articles.description: The oldest pair of compact quasars ever observed has been found only 900 million years after the Big Bang. Scientists say there is no theoretical explanation for how the pair of actively feeding black holes grew so massive at such an early time in the history of the universe. The pair of quasars has been given the Hawaiian nickname Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The oldest known compact quasar pair, observed just 900 million years after the Big Bang, poses intriguing questions about early black hole growth. This discovery reshapes our understanding of the early universe's rapid evolution.

articles.title: A massive new simulation reveals how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A groundbreaking new supercomputer simulation is revealing how the universe escaped its cosmic dark age and transformed into a cosmos filled with stars and galaxies. Called Lumina, it recreates 2 billion years of early cosmic history across a region 1.6 billion light-years wide, capturing extraordinary details that previous simulations could not.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking supercomputer simulation reveals how the universe transformed from its dark age into the luminous cosmos we observe today. This computational breakthrough illuminates one of cosmology's greatest mysteries.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA has unveiled an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing lunar landers. This ambitious timeline marks a new era of sustained human lunar exploration.

articles.title: Astronomers discover hidden alien planet in James Webb images
articles.description: A breakthrough in telescope imaging could reveal countless alien worlds that have been hiding in plain sight. Scientists developed a new technique that uses a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to remove the overwhelming glare of stars, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to detect than with conventional methods. The technology has already uncovered a previously hidden planet in existing telescope data and could reveal many more.
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a previously hidden alien planet using James Webb Space Telescope imagery, with techniques that could reveal countless additional exoplanets. This breakthrough opens new pathways for detecting worlds concealed in existing astronomical data.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's historic milestone of traveling one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch, inviting public participation in commemorative activities.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy.  […]
articles.summary: NASA scientists demonstrate how the upcoming LISA observatory will detect gravitational waves to reveal previously undiscovered worlds and deepen our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: Planets Don't Just Disappear, But They Can Wobble Out of Sight if Their Neighbour is Close Enough
articles.description: TESS watched an exoplanet about 1,000 light years away as it repeatedly transited in front of its star for seven years. But astronomers were surprised to find that the hot Jupiter disappeared. Of course, planets don't just disappear. Something interrupted its transits from our point of view, and astronomers think they've figured out what happened. An unseen, nearby giant planet companion tugged on it until TESS couldn't see it anymore.
articles.summary: TESS observations reveal that exoplanets can experience orbital wobbling caused by nearby planetary neighbors, demonstrating dynamic multi-planet system interactions over years of study.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: NOM4D and other emerging technologies demonstrate that automated assembly in space is rapidly maturing, enabling construction of large structures beyond Earth's gravity.

articles.title: Europe's Hera spacecraft begins close inspections of an asteroid rammed by NASA in a 2022 test
articles.description: A European spacecraft has begun close inspections of an asteroid rammed by NASA four years ago in a planetary defense test.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft is conducting detailed inspections of an asteroid following NASA's successful 2022 planetary defense test impact. This follow-up mission validates humanity's ability to protect Earth from asteroid threats.

articles.title: Centaurus A in the spotlight: Plasma simulations reproduce black hole jets' mysterious bright edges
articles.description: Around 12 million light-years away, the supermassive black hole of the galaxy Centaurus A is hurling two enormous plasma jets into space at nearly the speed of light. These so-called jets are brighter at their edges than at their center. The reason for this was previously unclear but has now been explained by a team from the Chair of Astronomy at the University of Würzburg. The research is published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Advanced plasma simulations now reproduce the mysterious bright edges of black hole jets from Centaurus A, located 12 million light-years away. This breakthrough deepens our understanding of supermassive black hole behavior.

articles.title: Bennu asteroid analysis suggests unexpected origins for organics in space
articles.description: Samples from the Bennu asteroid, which is currently more than 200 million miles (322 million kilometers) from Earth, and the Murchison meteorite, which fell to Earth in 1969, both contain molecules that build proteins necessary for life. New research has found that the molecules may have formed through the same process but originated far from one another in the solar system.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Analysis of samples from the Bennu asteroid suggests organic compounds in space may have unexpected origins. This discovery from NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission advances our knowledge of chemistry beyond Earth.

articles.title: How ripples in space-time can reveal new exoplanets
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets—worlds beyond our solar system—throughout our galaxy.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The upcoming LISA observatory will detect gravitational waves to identify new exoplanets, revealing worlds through ripples in space-time. This innovative detection method will expand our ability to discover distant planets.

articles.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe discovers a hidden pattern in the Sun’s chaotic magnetic fields
articles.description: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has revealed a surprising secret hidden within the chaos of space: turbulent magnetic fields reverse their direction of rotation when examined at extremely small scales. The discovery exposes an unexpected pattern in solar wind turbulence that could help scientists better understand solar activity and predict geomagnetic storms.
articles.summary: NASA's Parker Solar Probe has discovered hidden patterns in the Sun's turbulent magnetic fields, revealing order within apparent chaos. This discovery advances our understanding of solar physics and space weather.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech-developed robot has made history by autonomously building a structure in space, demonstrating breakthrough capabilities for future construction in orbit. This achievement opens possibilities for large-scale space infrastructure development.

articles.title: A radical theory says the universe is twice as old as we thought
articles.description: A provocative new cosmological model suggests the Universe could be 26.7 billion years old and might not need dark matter or dark energy to explain its behavior. University of Ottawa researchers tested the theory against several major astronomical observations, finding that it could explain galaxy rotation, cosmic expansion, and the formation of early elements.
articles.summary: A new cosmological model proposes the universe could be 26.7 billion years old, potentially eliminating the need for dark matter in current theories. This radical reimagining of cosmic age challenges our fundamental understanding of universal history.

articles.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
articles.description: NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for Mars Sample Return (MSR), called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture.
articles.summary: NASA has initiated a new phase of the Mars Sample Return mission, introducing the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture to bring Martian samples back to Earth. This ambitious program represents a major step toward understanding Mars' geology and past habitability.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA has opened applications for astronauts to live and work on the Moon, representing a major milestone in humanity's return to lunar exploration. This opportunity marks the beginning of sustained human presence on another celestial body.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have discovered evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, marking a significant breakthrough in understanding fundamental physics. This finding brings scientists closer to uncovering exotic particles in the zeptoverse, the realm of subatomic scales.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: New gravitational-wave observations have provided constraints on supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn, offering insights into the early universe. This research advances our understanding of how the universe's most extreme objects formed and evolved.

articles.title: Tras un año de espera en el espacio la misión ESCAPADE de la NASA pone por fin rumbo a Marte usando la gravedad de la Tierra
articles.description: Tras casi un año justo en el espacio las dos sondas de la misión ESCAPADE de la NASA utilizaron estos días la gravedad de la Tierra para coger impulso hacia Marte, su destino definitivo. En concreto ESCAPADE Blue llevó a cabo su máxima aproximación el sábado …
articles.summary: NASA's ESCAPADE mission has used Earth's gravity to propel its twin spacecraft toward Mars after nearly a year in space. This innovative maneuver demonstrates sophisticated mission planning for exploring the Red Planet's atmosphere.

articles.title: Les mystères de Mercure, ou comment la sonde BepiColombo va étudier la planète la plus proche du Soleil (sans tomber dedans)
articles.description: Après une mise en orbite d’une exquise complexité, la sonde européenne BepiColombo a un programme chargé. En effet, de nombreux mystères entourant la planète Mercure résistent toujours aux scientifiques.
articles.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft, after an intricately complex orbital insertion, is embarking on a comprehensive study of Mercury to unlock the mysteries of our solar system's innermost planet. This European mission will reveal crucial insights about planetary formation and extreme environments.

articles.title: Voici comment la NASA compte coloniser la Lune dans six ans
articles.description: La NASA compte bien établir une base permanente sur la Lune. Elle a dévoilé son plan, point par point.
articles.summary: NASA has unveiled its strategic plan to establish a permanent lunar base within six years, marking an ambitious milestone in humanity's return to the Moon. This comprehensive roadmap details how the space agency will achieve sustained lunar colonization.

articles.title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 5063-5069 Rocks and Chips
articles.description: Written by William Farrand, Senior Research Scientist, Space Science Institute Earth planning date: Friday, Nov. 6, 2026 This week Curiosity has been completing its drill campaign at the “Nazca” drill hole. This is an area characterized by bedrock containing disk-shaped (or in a liberal interpretation, potato chip shaped … see linked image) crystal forms. A […]
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover continues its exploration of Mars, analyzing rock samples and geological features during sols 5063-5069 of its ongoing mission.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: […]
articles.summary: NGC 4449, a small dwarf galaxy, demonstrates outsized astronomical influence through its interactions and star formation, revealing the dynamic nature of galactic systems.

articles.title: The Ice Giants' Magnetic Fields are Very Strange Compared to Earth's
articles.description: Uranus and Neptune, the Solar System's ice giants, have interiors unlike the other planets. As a result, they also have magnetic fields unlike the others. They're messy and tilted, and Voyager 2, the only spacecraft to even flyby them, showed us how messy they are. New research uses models to try to understand what's going on with the pair of planets and their weird fields, and found that it's likely they change on very short timescales. They could already be much different than when Voyager 2 visited in the late 1980s.
articles.summary: Uranus and Neptune's unusual magnetic fields, driven by their exotic planetary interiors, challenge our understanding of ice giants and magnetic phenomena.

articles.title: Asteroid Mining Will Crash the Platinum Market, But That’s Good News for Earth
articles.description: Science fiction authors have been dreaming of robotic spacecraft harvesting fortunes from asteroids for decades. Humanity is slowly getting closer to that reality. But if you ask asteroid mining skeptics, they will usually ask one specific question - what happens to the prices of all those rare materials once someone actually brings them back? A pair of system dynamicists from MIT directly tackled that question with a new paper titled Will AstroForge Collapse the PGM Market?
articles.summary: Future asteroid mining operations promise to deliver abundant resources to Earth while fundamentally transforming commodity markets in beneficial ways for humanity.

articles.title: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory Unmasks a Supernova Impostor
articles.description: Some stars, called Luminous Blue Variables, can be confused with supernovae explosions. They exhibit similar outbursts, but unlike supernovae, which explode once and then are gone forever, these stars have periodic outbursts. New research found that one of these 'supernova impostors' is in a binary relationship with a black hole or a neutron star, and that explains its periodic outbursts.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-Ray Observatory helps astronomers distinguish between Luminous Blue Variables and supernovae by revealing the distinct characteristics of these stellar phenomena.

articles.title: ALMA Reveals a Jet of Cool Gas from a Microquasar
articles.description: There's a strange gamma-ray emitter in the Large Magellanic Cloud that has astronomers stumped about its source. It lies within the ashes left behind by a supernova that created a compact object that's part of the system. The supernova remnant provides some evidence for the emissions, but not the whole story.
articles.summary: ALMA observations reveal a cool gas jet from a mysterious gamma-ray emitting microquasar in the Large Magellanic Cloud, deepening astronomers' understanding of these exotic objects.
